triggers: You want the Notion consent prompt and page picker to name your product instead of a shared connection (inferred from the generic branding trigger).
You plan a Notion Marketplace listing: only a public connection with installation scope "Any workspace" is eligible, and the scope can't be changed after creation.
ownApp.notes: Composio lists Notion as a Composio-managed OAuth toolkit. Your own public connection is free and needs no review. Pick the installation scope carefully: it is set once at creation. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard (Create Auth Config); don't hard-code it.

verdict.summary: Instant: create a public connection in the developer portal with no review. The catch is per-user, per-page grants: each user picks pages in a page picker, and the agent sees nothing else.

milestones.definition: You can authorize the connection in your development workspace and call the API with the returned token.

limitsUntilNext.value: With installation scope "Selected workspaces only", only the workspaces you picked at creation can install it.

sources.quote: Selected workspaces only Only the workspaces you select at creation time.

milestones.definition: Users in other workspaces can install the connection and grant pages.
Any Notion user can install the connection. No Notion review is needed; a Marketplace listing is a separate, optional step.

gates.name: Create a public connection in the developer portal

requirements.label: Notion account and a development workspace
requirements.detail: You choose the development workspace when creating the connection.

requirements.label: Decide installation scope up front
requirements.detail: "Any workspace" (Marketplace-eligible) or "Selected workspaces only". It can't be changed later; changing it means creating a new connection.

requirements.label: Redirect URI
requirements.detail: From the Composio dashboard if you use Composio.

scopes.name: Capabilities: read content
scopes.whyNeeded: Notion uses capabilities, not OAuth scope strings. Read content lets the agent read the pages the user granted.
scopes.reviewTrigger: None. Users see the capabilities on the consent prompt.

scopes.name: Capabilities: update / insert content
scopes.whyNeeded: Write back to granted pages and databases.
scopes.reviewTrigger: None. Shown to the user on the consent prompt.

steps.title: Pick installation scope and capabilities
actions: Choose "Any workspace" if you might ever list on the Marketplace.
Enable only the capabilities the agent uses.
steps.doneWhen: Scope and capability list are written down.

steps.title: Create the public connection
actions: Developer portal → Build → Public connections → Create new connection.
Fill connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities.

steps.title: Copy credentials into Composio
actions: Configuration tab → copy OAuth client ID and client secret.
In Composio, Create Auth Config → Notion, paste them, and pass the auth config ID in your session.
steps.doneWhen: A Composio session uses your auth config ID for notion.

steps.title: Authorize and confirm page scoping
actions: Authorize from a second workspace and grant one page.
Confirm the agent can read that page and gets an error on an ungranted page.

redirectUris.value: Register one or more redirect URIs on the connection; Notion redirects there with the code or an error parameter.

sources.quote: If the user denies access, they are redirected to the redirect_uri with an error query parameter.

pkce.value: Not mentioned in the authorization guide; the token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth with the client secret.
pkce.note: Absence in the docs we fetched, not a confirmed lack of support.

refresh.value: The token response includes a refresh_token used to get a new access_token.

sources.quote: The refresh_token will be used to refresh the access token, which generates a new access_token .

rateLimits.value: Per connection: 600 requests/minute on Business and Enterprise workspaces, 180 requests/minute on all other plans. A per-workspace limit also applies.

sources.quote: Business and Enterprise 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) All other plans 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)

blockers.description: The agent only sees pages each user picks in the OAuth page picker, and every workspace member must authorize separately. Agents expecting workspace-wide access find nothing.
blockers.workaround: Tell users which pages to grant during onboarding, or offer a Notion template in the auth flow.

blockers.description: Installation scope is fixed at creation. "Selected workspaces only" connections can't list on the Marketplace.
blockers.workaround: Create a new connection with "Any workspace".

agentTasks: Fill the connection form in a logged-in browser.
Draft onboarding copy telling users which pages to grant.
Verify page-grant scoping with a test call.
humanTasks: Log in to Notion and choose the development workspace.

unknowns: PKCE support: not documented in the pages we fetched.
Access and refresh token lifetimes: not stated in the authorization guide.

Notion Marketplace listing review process and timeline (optional path; not researched).

evidence.claim: Create new connection asks for name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.
evidence.quote: Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including: Connection name and development workspace Redirect URI(s) for the OAuth flow

evidence.claim: Installation scope is set once and can't be changed.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can’t be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: Users pick pages during authorization, and each workspace member authorizes separately.
evidence.quote: If multiple members in a workspace want to use the same public connection, each user needs to complete the authorization flow individually.

evidence.claim: The token response includes a refresh_token.
evidence.quote: Notion responds to the request with an access_token , refresh_token , and additional information.

evidence.claim: Per-connection rate limits depend on the workspace plan.
evidence.quote: Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace’s plan

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint redirects to app.notion.com/install-integration.
For OAuth toolkits, the Composio dashboard shows the redirect URI to register with the provider.
evidence.quote: For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.

corrections.before: An average of three requests per second per connection.
corrections.after: Per connection, per 60-second window: 600/min on Business and Enterprise, 180/min (about 3/s) on other plans, plus a per-workspace limit.
corrections.reason: Notion's request-limits page now ties the budget to the workspace plan.
